description: Immerse yourself in the rustic charm of Focaccia Genovese, a beloved Italian flatbread from Liguria. This recipe delivers a perfectly crisp crust, a tender, airy crumb, and the irresistible aroma of fresh rosemary and rich olive oil. It is a simple pleasure that transports you straight to the sun-drenched coasts of Genoa.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water, sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the strong bread flour, fine sea salt, and 60ml of extra virgin olive oil to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms and all the flour is incorporated. The dough will be quite wet.

instructions.title: Knead and Develop Gluten
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface. Knead for 10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with a dough hook for 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place the kneaded dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat with oil. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape and Second Rise
instructions.text: Pour 30ml of extra virgin olive oil onto a 9x13 inch baking sheet, ensuring the entire surface is coated. Gently transfer the risen dough to the oiled sheet. Using your fingertips, gently dimple the dough all over, pressing down to create characteristic indentations. Sprinkle with fresh rosemary leaves. Cover loosely and let it rise again for 30-45 minutes.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Just before baking, sprinkle the dough generously with coarse sea salt. Bake for 25-35 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and cooked through.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven. If desired, drizzle with a little more fresh extra virgin olive oil for extra flavor. Let it cool on a wire rack for a few minutes before slicing and serving warm. Buon appetito!

tips: Do not be afraid to dimple the dough deeply with your fingertips; this creates the characteristic texture and pockets for the olive oil to pool and flavor the bread.
Always use good quality extra virgin olive oil, especially for the topping, as its rich, fruity flavor is central to authentic Focaccia Genovese.
Focaccia is best enjoyed warm on the day it is baked. If you have leftovers, refresh them briefly in a warm oven or toaster for a few minutes to restore its crispness.
article:
Focaccia Genovese: A Taste of Italian Sunshine with Rosemary and Olive Oil

Imagine a golden-crusted bread, fragrant with rosemary, glistening with olive oil, and boasting an irresistibly airy, tender crumb. This isn't just any bread; it's Focaccia Genovese, a culinary masterpiece from the Ligurian coast of Italy. More than a simple side, this iconic flatbread is a testament to the beauty of simple, high-quality ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. If you're searching for the perfect Focaccia Genovese recipe to bring the authentic taste of Italian baking to your kitchen, you've come to the right place. Get ready to embark on a delicious journey that will elevate your baking skills and delight your taste buds.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?

Focaccia Genovese, or *Fügassa* in the local Genoese dialect, is a traditional flatbread originating from Genoa, the capital of Italy's Liguria region. Unlike its thicker, bread-like cousins from other parts of Italy, authentic Focaccia Genovese is characterized by its relatively thin profile, incredibly soft and airy interior, and a distinctively dimpled surface that creates little pockets for olive oil and coarse sea salt. The dough is enriched with generous amounts of extra virgin olive oil, which contributes to its unique flavor and texture, resulting in a crust that's crisp on the outside and wonderfully chewy within. Often adorned with fresh rosemary, this rustic yet refined bread is a staple in Ligurian bakeries and homes, enjoyed at any time of day – from breakfast dipped in coffee to an afternoon snack or a delightful accompaniment to meals. Crafting this classic Focaccia Genovese recipe is a must-try for any baking enthusiast.

## Ingredients You Need for Focaccia Genovese

The magic of Focaccia Genovese lies in the quality and simplicity of its ingredients. Gathering the right components is key to a successful Focaccia Genovese recipe that truly captures its authentic essence.

*   **"00" Flour or Strong Bread Flour (approx. 500g):** "00" flour is ideal for its fine texture, resulting in a tender crumb. If unavailable, a high-quality strong bread flour with a protein content of 12-14% will also work beautifully.
*   **Lukewarm Water (approx. 350-380ml):** The exact amount can vary slightly depending on your flour and humidity. It should feel warm to the touch, not hot, to activate the yeast without killing it.
*   **Active Dry Yeast (7g or 1 sachet):** Ensures a light and airy texture.
*   **Fine Sea Salt (10g for the dough, plus extra for topping):** Essential for flavor balance in the dough and the signature salty crunch on top.
*   **Granulated Sugar (5g, optional):** A pinch helps to activate the yeast more quickly.
*   **High-Quality Extra Virgin Olive Oil (at least 60-80ml for the dough, plus plenty for the pan and topping):** This is non-negotiable. Use the best olive oil you can find, as its flavor is central to the focaccia.
*   **Fresh Rosemary (2-3 sprigs):** For its aromatic fragrance and beautiful presentation.
*   **For the Brine (optional but highly recommended):** 2 tablespoons water, 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt. This mixture creates the characteristic salty, crisp top.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Focaccia Genovese

Creating this delightful bread is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a truly authentic Focaccia Genovese recipe:

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water, sugar (if using), and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and 10g of fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Stir with a wooden spoon or a Danish dough whisk until a shaggy dough forms.
3.  **Add Olive Oil & Knead:** Pour in about 60ml of extra virgin olive oil. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 5-7 minutes. The dough will be quite sticky initially but will become smoother and more elastic as you knead. Resist the urge to add too much flour. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with a dough hook on medium speed for 5-6 minutes.
4.  **First Proof (Bulk Fermentation):** Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place the dough in the bowl, turn it once to coat, and cover with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel. Let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally coat a 9x13 inch (or similar size) baking pan with extra virgin olive oil – don't be shy! This prevents sticking and contributes to the crispy bottom.
6.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently deflate the dough and transfer it to the oiled baking pan. Using your fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan. If it resists, let it rest for 10-15 minutes and then continue stretching. You want an even layer.
7.  **Second Proof:** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
8.  **Dimple and Top:** Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Once the dough has risen, uncover it. Dip your fingers in olive oil and create deep dimples all over the surface, pressing all the way down to the bottom of the pan. This is crucial for the signature texture. Drizzle more olive oil generously over the top.
9.  **Add Brine & Rosemary:** If making the brine, whisk together 2 tablespoons of water, 1 tablespoon of olive oil, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Drizzle this mixture evenly over the dimpled focaccia. Scatter fresh rosemary sprigs over the top and sprinkle with a final pinch of coarse sea salt.
10. **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the bottom is crisp and golden.
11. **Cool:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia from the pan to a wire rack to cool slightly. Serve warm or at room temperature.

## Pro Tips for the Best Focaccia Genovese

Mastering this Focaccia Genovese recipe comes down to a few key techniques and quality choices:

*   **Quality Olive Oil is Paramount:** This cannot be stressed enough. The flavor of your focaccia heavily relies on the quality of your extra virgin olive oil. Use a good one for both the dough and the generous topping.
*   **Hydration is Key:** Focaccia dough is a high-hydration dough, meaning it's quite wet and sticky. Resist the urge to add too much flour during kneading, as this will result in a dry, dense focaccia. A sticky dough yields an airy crumb.
*   **Don't Fear the Oil in the Pan:** A well-oiled pan is essential for a crispy, golden bottom crust and prevents sticking. Be generous!
*   **Deep Dimples:** When dimpling the dough, don't be shy! Press your fingers deeply into the dough. These pockets hold the precious olive oil and brine, contributing to the focaccia's unique texture and flavor.
*   **The Brine is a Game-Changer:** While optional, the water, olive oil, and salt brine drizzled over the top before baking creates that characteristic slightly chewy, salty, and incredibly flavorful crust that sets Genovese focaccia apart.
*   **Proper Proofing:** Allow the dough to proof sufficiently in a warm, draft-free environment. This develops flavor and ensures a light, airy texture.

## Serving Suggestions for Focaccia Genovese

Once you've perfected your Focaccia Genovese recipe, the ways to enjoy it are endless. Its versatility makes it a perfect addition to almost any meal or occasion.

*   **As an Appetizer:** Serve warm, plain, or with a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping.
*   **Charcuterie and Cheese Board:** Focaccia Genovese is a superb accompaniment to a selection of Italian cured meats, cheeses, and olives.
*   **Sandwich Base:** Slice it horizontally and fill with prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, roasted vegetables, or pesto for an incredible Italian sandwich.
*   **With Soups and Salads:** Its hearty yet light texture makes it perfect for soaking up broths or complementing a crisp green salad.
*   **Breakfast or Snack:** In Genoa, it's often enjoyed for breakfast, sometimes even dipped in coffee! It also makes a wonderful mid-afternoon snack.
*   **With Wine:** A simple slice of focaccia with a glass of crisp white Ligurian wine like Vermentino is pure bliss.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Focaccia Genovese with rosemary and olive oil is perfection in itself, you can explore subtle variations:

*   **Other Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, you can experiment with fresh thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Toppings:** Before the final dimpling and baking, you can add thin slices of cherry tomatoes, pitted olives, thinly sliced onions, or even a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese (though less traditional for Genovese style).
*   **Flour Blends:** For a slightly different texture, you could substitute a small portion (e.g., 50-100g) of the "00" flour with whole wheat flour, though this will result in a denser crumb.
*   **Garlic:** Infuse some of your olive oil with thinly sliced garlic before drizzling it over the focaccia for an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Sweet Focaccia (Focaccia Dolce):** While not Genovese, some regions make sweet versions with sugar, raisins, or fresh fruit. This is a departure from the savory classic but a fun experiment.

Focaccia Genovese is more than just bread; it's an experience. Its simplicity belies a depth of flavor and texture that truly embodies the heart of Italian baking. By following this Focaccia Genovese recipe, you're not just making bread; you're creating a piece of culinary heritage that will bring joy to your table. Embark on your journey to master the Focaccia Genovese recipe today, and prepare to be amazed by the delicious results.
